subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron agentTurn runs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` layer, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This choice defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and a public security/config contract, so automation should not choose precedence or compatibility semantics.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron runs reuse `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface while coupling two distinct execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Document that operators must use per-job `toolsAllow` and delivery safeguards instead of a global cron policy.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against existing policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest issue-specific review history and recent cron/tool-policy routing signal.
